[.tooling/components/apis/rating-service/k8s/README.md#rating-service-kubernetes-manifests]

# Rating Service Kubernetes Manifests

This directory contains Kubernetes manifests for deploying the Rating Service to EKS.
page_texts.2:
[.tooling/components/apis/rating-service/k8s/README.md#files]

## Files

- `postgres-cluster.yaml` - CloudNativePG PostgreSQL cluster (3 replicas with HA)
- `configmap.yaml` - Environment configuration
- `secret.yaml` - Database credentials (sensitive data)
- `deployment.yaml` - Service deployment with 2 replicas
- `service.yaml` - ClusterIP service exposing HTTPS on port 8443
- `INFRASTRUCTURE.md` - Detailed infrastructure setup guide
page_texts.4:
[.tooling/components/apis/rating-service/k8s/README.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

1. CloudNativePG operator installed in cluster
2. Namespace created: `kubectl create namespace eapref-app`
3. S3 bucket for PostgreSQL backups
page_texts.5:
[.tooling/components/apis/rating-service/k8s/README.md#deploy-in-order]

### Deploy (in order)

```bash
# Set environment variables
export NAMESPACE=eapref-app
export IMAGE_URI=<your-ecr-uri>/rating-service:latest
export BUCKET_NAME=your-backup-bucket

# 1. Deploy PostgreSQL cluster first
envsubst < postgres-cluster.yaml | kubectl apply -f -

# Wait for database to be ready (2-3 minutes)
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready cluster/rating-postgres -n ${NAMESPACE} --timeout=5m

# 2. Deploy application
kubectl apply -f configmap.yaml
kubectl apply -f secret.yaml
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml
kubectl apply -f service.yaml
```
page_texts.6:
[.tooling/components/apis/rating-service/k8s/README.md#update-shared-ingress]

### Update Shared Ingress

The rating service path has been added to the shared ingress in the RAG service:

```bash
export EKS_INGRESS_HOST=ea-reference.shared.dev.pgwcloud.net
export NAMESPACE=eapref-app

cd ../../rag-service
envsubst < k8s/ingress.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

[.tooling/components/apis/rating-service/k8s/README.md#verify-deployment]

### Verify Deployment

```bash
# Check pod status
kubectl get pods -n ${NAMESPACE} -l app=rating-service

# Check service
kubectl get svc -n ${NAMESPACE} rating-service

# Check logs
kubectl logs -n ${NAMESPACE} -l app=rating-service -f

# Test health endpoint
kubectl exec -n ${NAMESPACE} -it deployment/rating-service -- \
  curl -k https://localhost:8443/api/rating/v1/health
```

## Database Setup

The rating service expects a PostgreSQL database with the following configuration:

- Database name: `ratings`
- User: `application_user`
- Tables: Created automatically via SQLAlchemy on startup

[.tooling/components/apis/rating-service/k8s/README.md#security-notes]

## Security Notes

- Secret values are base64-encoded, not encrypted
- Use sealed-secrets or external-secrets for production
- Database password should be rotated regularly
- HTTPS-only communication with self-signed certificates
